neighboring_unit_entries.title: The I+ continuum equation becomes scattering from the derivative of the running coupling
neighboring_unit_entries.why_material: Introducing an integrated wavefunction converts the nonlocal threshold equation into a second-order ODE; an adapted coordinate and gauge transformation expose an effective Schrödinger Hamiltonian with potential V+=(1/2)dg_D/dq and explicit boundary conditions.

neighboring_unit_entries.title: Statewise solvability does not automatically extend to many-body integrability
neighboring_unit_entries.why_material: Limits the exact correspondence: multiple rapidities obstruct a direct many-body I→RD map, and level-dependent boundary couplings suggest a more complicated transfer-matrix structure rather than an established integrable theory.

related_synthesis_entries.claim: Smooth arctangent contributions explain why perturbing or deleting levels fails to model irregular zero fluctuations; imposing RG closure instead selects two level-dependent coupling patterns whose gradients become partner scattering potentials.
related_synthesis_entries.limit: The source proposes the scattering connection but gives neither discrete exact eigenvalue equations for I± nor a construction reproducing the zeros.

   On more general grounds, let us recall that one of the motivations to consider the Hamil-
tonian xp was the breaking of time reversal symmetry, which should be related to the GUE
statistics of the zeros. This Hamiltonian gives an accurate semiclassical description of them
but not of their fluctuations. The I± models break time reversal, but they also break the
reversal of the RG time direction. Could this additional breaking be related to the GUE
statistics of the zeros?
